stories.title: Mass Shootings in South Africa Leave 27 Dead in Separate Incidents
stories.summary: Two mass shootings occurred hours apart in South Africa, resulting in at least 27 fatalities. The first incident took place at a tavern near Johannesburg, where 17 people were killed by gunmen armed with assault rifles. The second shooting, which left 10 dead, happened at a barbecue venue near Cape Town. Police are investigating potential links to gang violence and illegal mining turf wars, with no arrests made so far.

stories.title: Five Arrested in Terrorism Investigation Near U.K. Air Base Used by U.S. Forces
stories.summary: British police arrested five men on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses near RAF Fairford, a U.K. air base used by U.S. forces. The arrests occurred after reports of three suspicious vehicles heading toward the military airfield. Homes in the vicinity were evacuated as bomb disposal teams conducted investigations.

stories.title: Trump Dismisses Iran's Proposal to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week and resume nuclear negotiations. Trump stated that the deal was not acceptable, expressing a desire for a better agreement. Iranian officials, while aware of Trump's comments, noted they had not received a formal rejection of the plan. Iran's Foreign Minister indicated that the country is prepared for renewed conflict but remains open to diplomatic solutions.

stories.summary: The Republic of Ireland football team plans to wear black armbands during their upcoming match against Israel to honor all lives lost in the Gaza conflict. stories.title: Explosion in Athens' Plaka District Kills Six, Including Four American Tourists
stories.summary: A suspected gas leak caused an explosion that leveled a two-storey residential building in the Plaka district of Athens, resulting in the deaths of six individuals, including four American tourists and two Greek residents. Emergency teams discovered the victims after the building collapsed shortly after the explosion, which occurred early in the morning. Greek authorities are investigating the incident to determine the cause of the explosion.

stories.title: Swiss Voters Reject Stricter Neutrality Rules in Referendum
stories.summary: Swiss voters have decisively rejected a proposal to impose stricter limits on the country's neutrality, with early projections indicating that approximately 71 percent opposed the initiative. Neutrality has been a key principle in Switzerland since it was enshrined in the constitution in 1848.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV Visits Lourdes, Addresses Clergy Abuse and Healing
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV is on a four-day visit to France, having recently prayed at the Grotto of Massabielle in Lourdes, a significant pilgrimage site. He is set to meet privately with survivors of clerical sexual abuse, following a French inquiry that revealed extensive abuse within the Church. During his visit, the Pope emphasized the need for the Church to confront its past and heal 'deep wounds' while also criticizing assisted dying as 'false compassion.'

This statement comes in the context of recent legislation in France that established a right to assisted dying for certain adults with incurable conditions.

stories.title: Belfast Court Upholds Orange Order Parade Through Catholic Area

The ruling came during an unprecedented late-night court session, following several last-minute legal challenges.
